about: Richmond's car lines in 1925, as Harland Bartholomew & Associates drew them for the City Planning Commission (plate 53, 'Early Transit Routes, 1888 & 1925', 31 January 1943), within the city limits of the day, plus the interurban to Ashland, which ran on its own. The plate is a small diagram: each line here follows the streets it names, placed on today's OpenStreetMap streets, with the details from the sources given per line. Where a source is silent, a line's ends are approximate; the notes say which.

routes.name: Westhampton line
routes.note: West on Floyd Avenue from Robinson Street to the belt line railroad, under it in a tunnel, then a little north to Grove Avenue; out Grove to Three Chopt Road; then on its own right-of-way beside Three Chopt to Towana Road, and on (the line of today's Campus Drive) to Westhampton Park, which became the University of Richmond's campus in 1914. The right-of-way beside Three Chopt is drawn along the road itself.

routes.name: Belmont line
routes.route: Broad Street – Sheppard Street – Cary Street – Belmont Avenue
routes.note: The Broad Street line's extension west from Robinson Street to Sheppard, south to Cary, later carried on eleven blocks to Garrett Street. Which street carried the last stretch is read from the 1925 plate's 'Belmont' label.

routes.name: Broad Street line
routes.route: Broad Street, Sheppard Street to Church Hill
routes.note: Broad Street, the spine of the system, from the Belmont line's turn at Sheppard Street east to Church Hill. The east end is approximate.

routes.name: State Fair Grounds spur
routes.route: Boulevard north to the Fair Grounds
routes.note: The 1925 plate shows a short spur north from Broad Street ending in a loop. It is drawn here up the Boulevard to the State Fair Grounds (1906–1941, on the site of The Diamond); which street the spur took is not certain.

routes.name: Main Street line
routes.route: Main Street, Robinson Street to Shockoe
routes.note: West Main Street, which the line turned into a commercial street through the Fan, east to Shockoe. The west end is approximate.

routes.name: Harrison Street line
routes.note: A crosstown link on Harrison Street between the Main, Floyd and Broad lines, as the 1925 plate shows it.

routes.name: Reservoir (Byrd) Park line
routes.note: Down Robinson Street to Reservoir Park (Byrd Park), one of the trolley's favourite destinations, along Lakeview Avenue as the 1925 plate labels it. The far end is approximate.

routes.name: Clay Street line
routes.note: Sprague's first line of 1888 ran from Church Hill to Clay and Hancock Streets; the 1925 plate still shows Clay Street. The ends are approximate.

routes.name: Brookland and Lakeside line
routes.route: 1st Street – North Avenue – Brookland Park – Chamberlayne – Laburnum – Hermitage Road
routes.note: Over the First Street viaduct (1891) into Barton Heights, then west along Brookland Park Boulevard, north up the median of Chamberlayne Avenue, west on Laburnum and north on Hermitage Road to Lakeside Park and Lewis Ginter's Lakeside Wheel Club. The run beyond Hermitage Road along Lakeside Avenue is approximate.

routes.name: Highland Park line
routes.route: 5th Street – Northside Viaduct – Highland Park loop
routes.note: North on Fifth Street over the Northside Viaduct (1892) to Chestnut Hill and Highland Park, and after 1908 round a loop by Meadowbridge Road, Milton Street and Highland Street (the cross street joining them, Second Avenue here, is approximate). The Hull Street–Highland Park line was Richmond's last: the last car ran on 25 November 1949.

routes.name: Marshall Street line (Fulton)
routes.route: Marshall Street Viaduct – Church Hill – Fulton
routes.note: Across Shockoe Valley on the Marshall Street Viaduct (1911, since demolished: drawn straight) from College Street to 21st Street at Jefferson Park, out Marshall Street, and down to Fulton along Williamsburg Avenue. The route from Marshall Street down to Fulton is approximate.

routes.name: Venable Street line
routes.route: 17th Street – Venable Street – 25th Street – Nine Mile Road
routes.note: North on 17th Street, east along Venable Street through Union Hill, and up 25th Street to Nine Mile Road, the road the Seven Pines line took out of the city (chartered along 25th to 29th Streets and Nine Mile Road). The federal government bought the Seven Pines line in 1918 for a wartime plant; how far cars ran out Nine Mile Road in 1925 is not certain.

routes.name: Jefferson Avenue line
routes.note: Up 21st Street and out Jefferson Avenue past Jefferson Park, one of the trolley's pleasure grounds, as the 1925 plate shows it.

routes.name: Hull Street line
routes.note: Over the Mayo Bridge into Manchester and out Hull Street. Its last car, No. 408 on the Hull Street–Highland Park run, ended Richmond's streetcars on 25 November 1949. The outer end is approximate.

routes.name: Forest Hill line
routes.route: 7th Street – Free Bridge – Semmes Avenue – Forest Hill Avenue
routes.note: South over the river (the free bridge at Ninth Street), down the median of Semmes Avenue through Woodland Heights, and out Forest Hill Avenue to Forest Hill Park and its amusement park, the most popular trolley destination of all. VEPCO proposed taking up the Semmes Avenue tracks in 1933.

routes.name: Richmond–Ashland Railway
routes.route: Broad and Laurel – Brook Road – Ashland
routes.note: The interurban to Ashland, built as the Richmond and Chesapeake Bay Railway (1907) and run as the Richmond–Ashland Railway from 1919 to 1938: from its terminal at Broad and Laurel Streets (814 West Broad), over a half-mile concrete trestle across Bacon's Quarter Branch (drawn straight), then up Brook Road and on to Ashland.
